questions.prompt: A thick morning fog shrouds a medieval muddy training ground near a stone castle. Three fully armored knights face off in a triangular formation, lances raised. At a herald's trumpet blast, two charge forward and clash with a forceful collision, mud splashing beneath their boots, one lance splintering on impact. The third knight circles behind and strikes the stumbling loser across the back with a mace, knocking him face-first into the mud. The remaining two engage in close combat — swords drawn, trading blows, each hit sending sparks and denting the metal surface. One disarms the other with a sweeping strike; the disarmed knight grabs a shield from the mud and blocks a downward slash. From the castle wall above, spectators cheer and a lady drops a red favor. The camera tracks low through the mud, capturing the metallic sheen of dented armor, breath misting in cold air, and blood mixing with muddy water. The victor raises his sword overhead, fog swirling around him.
